messages:
maya: heads-up: seeing repeated CUDA OOMs on pool-gamma nodes even though headroom shows ~1.2GB. Root-level alloc fails after reserve claim, node then flickers to 'degraded'. Triggered page to oncall. :warning:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 2026-03-15T12:34Z - high error rate on runtime pool-gamma - pages sent to oncall. Links: https://incidents.internal/1912345678
shawn: +1 seeing it. grabbing logs now. stack trace shows `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` from runtime allocator when trying to materialize KV-cache shards. weird part: allocator metrics report spare_pool and headroom > threshold, but actual cudaMalloc fails. suspect fragmentation + reserved-block alignment issue. :eyes:
li: pasting relevant log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T12:33:51Z] runtime_allocator: reserved_blocks=56 spare_pool=10 headroom_bytes=1298342400
[2026-03-15T12:33:51Z] runtime_allocator: active_allocations=2345 kv_cache_reserved_shards=18
[2026-03-15T12:33:52Z] cudaMemcpy Async -> ERROR: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2026-03-15T12:33:52Z] fallback: attempting spill-to-disk -> success
[2026-03-15T12:33:53Z] reserve_claim: fail: cannot reserve contiguous block (fragmentation)
```
maya: that `cannot reserve contiguous block` line matches fragmentation. I think the allocator's shadow reserves (we added last quarter) may not be releasing on partial spills. Could be silent leak where reserved_blocks counter stays high but headroom accounting still optimistic due to pre-reserved shadow pool.
priya: mitigation checklist incoming:
- run `runtimectl evict-kv --node pool-gamma-3 --shard-all` to free reserved shards on affected node (non-disruptive attempt)
- bump eviction aggressiveness: `runtimectl config set kv_evict_threshold 0.5` (was 0.75)
- temporarily disable prefix caching for heavy tenants: `route-config disable-prefix-cache tenant=acmeai`
- if still failing, schedule rolling restart of runtime container on node (graceful): `kubectl rollout restart ds/runtime -l pool=pool-gamma --grace-period=60`
shawn: running `runtimectl dump-allocator pool-gamma-3` now, will paste output. also checking if any long-running L2 spill tasks are stuck.
li: FYI you can also `echo 1 > /sys/module/nvidia_uvm/parameters/flush` on nodes to force reclamation of kernel-side reservations (only for debugging). use carefully.
shawn: dump pasted:
```
allocator_state {
  total_gpu_bytes: 17179869184
  free_bytes_reported: 2100000000
  contiguous_free_max: 420000000
  reserved_blocks_list: [64MB x 12, 32MB x 8, 8MB x 36]
  fragmented_free: 1650000000
  shadow_reserved_bytes: 480000000
}
```
priya: contiguous_free_max = 420MB but tries to alloc a 768MB contiguous block -> will fail even though sum(free) > requested. exactly fragmentation.
maya: quick mitigation path: 1) evict KV shards on nodes with highest shadow_reserved_bytes; 2) lower kv_evict_threshold to trigger more aggressive evictions; 3) scale up burst capacity to add empty nodes (temp) and route new requests there; 4) prepare fallback to smaller quantized model for heavy tenants (acmeai) if retries keep failing.
support-bot: customer-impact note: 12 failed inference requests from AcmeAI (eu-west-1) between 12:32-12:36Z; automated retries returned 503 in first attempt, ~7 retried successfully. ticket #INC-7342 created.
priya: sending short customer message draft to support: "We're investigating a transient resource fragmentation issue that caused a subset of inference requests to fail. We've implemented targeted evictions and are monitoring — expected resolution within 30-45 minutes. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary." any edits?
maya: good. add that we have automatic retries and retries likely succeeded for most requests. also mention no model state corruption.
shawn: evict step completed on pool-gamma-3: `evicted 13 shards freed ~420MB contiguous`. repeated `runtimectl dump-allocator` shows contiguous_free_max increased to ~740MB. trying a canary allocation now.
li: canary success: big allocation of 768MB succeeded on pool-gamma-3. :thumbsup:
maya: rolling evictions across remaining 3 nodes (one at a time) to avoid full capacity loss. starting with pool-gamma-1.
priya: also enabling routing fallback: heavy requests for tenant=acmeai will be routed to dedicated-burst-2 (smaller model) until we finish reclaim. config push in 2m.
shawn: note: container restarts weren't necessary so far. avoid restart unless evictions don't hold — restarts cause KV cache warmup and increased tail latency.
ops-bot: scheduled action: evict-kv on pool-gamma-1,2,4 in 120s intervals.
maya: taking first oncall handover now, will stay for 30m then hand to shawn for monitoring. shawn: I'll take the next 2h. priy­a: will pick up the postmortem and customer comms.
support-bot: support message sent to AcmeAI: "We've mitigated the immediate issue by freeing reserved memory and routing heavy requests to alternate pool. No data loss. We'll follow up with full RCA."
li: follow-ups for RCA: capture: per-node allocator histograms, shadow reserve accounting codepath, recent change that increased shadow reserve default from 256MB->512MB (rollout 2026-02-28). looks suspicious.
maya: action items:
- shawn/priya: create incident ticket with timeline + customer impact (assigned to priy­a)
- li: add reproduction test that simulates contiguous large alloc + heavy KV reservations to exercise fragmentation (owned)
- runtime-team: short-term config rollback plan for shadow reserve default if needed
- eng-sre: consider defrag job that runs low-priority compaction during off-peak windows

last update: 12:58Z - nodes stable, error rate back to baseline. leaving this thread open for RCA notes.
shawn: handing monitoring to oncall rotation, switching pager to follow-up.
maya: thanks all. :heart:
